label: Heavy, but easing
summary: The world rises to 39, still in the 'Bad' band but five points better, because the Gulf war stopped shooting for a weekend. The United States held off attacking Iran for a second straight day and Tehran said it had done the same, ending a run of nearly two weeks of nightly strikes; an Omani delegation shuttled through Tehran on Friday and Saturday trying to negotiate a provisional arrangement for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a regional official called the lull 'a positive signal,' and US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said Trump was giving talks 'some space' while the military stayed 'locked and loaded.' The pause is not a settlement: Iran's foreign ministry insisted it has no negotiations with Washington, the US naval blockade held with a dozen ships redirected and two boarded, the IRGC turned back six more vessels with warning shots, and Iranian media reported an oil tanker exploding on a naval mine after straying from Tehran's designated corridor. Israel's security cabinet gave initial approval for an International Stabilization Force of some 200 troops to enter Gaza, even as the IPC found 59 percent of Gazans in crisis-level hunger and projected two-thirds by year's end. Europe carried the day's weight. More than 250,000 people were out of their homes in France, the largest peacetime evacuation since the Second World War, with roughly 42,000 hectares burned in the Gironde and 75 firefighters treated, while Spain had 76,000 evacuated and one death near Valencia; hotter weather was forecast from Tuesday. In Berlin, police shot dead the 21-year-old who rammed a van into crowds near Saturday's Pride march and stabbed passers-by, killing one and injuring 29, in what the interior minister called an Islamist terror attack. Russia fired seven ballistic missiles and 136 drones at Kyiv overnight, and four civilians died in Ukraine and four more in Russian-held Horlivka. Africa's Ebola emergency kept accelerating past 3,000 cases and 1,350 deaths, though Oxford began testing a Bundibugyo vaccine on Friday and Sudan's army retook Bara, easing the siege of Al Obeid. Three people were shot dead at Seattle's Bite of Seattle festival, and 17 crew were missing after a Vietnamese cargo ship sank in the South China Sea, prompting a joint Vietnamese, Philippine and Chinese search. The lighter column was real: Tadej Pogacar won a record-equalling fifth Tour de France on a final stage shortened to free police for the fires, Soyuz MS-28 brought three crew home after 241 days, the Commonwealth Games ran on in Glasgow, and the week's tally included Brazilian Amazon deforestation at a ten-year low, down 38 percent, global road deaths down 21 percent since 2011 and a third straight annual fall in world hunger. Brazil recalled its ambassador to Buenos Aires after President Milei called President Lula a 'thief' at a rally. The headline matches the rubric formula with no adjustment.

drivers.headline: The United States and Iran pause attacks on each other for a second straight day, a hiatus that began Friday after nearly two weeks of intensifying US strikes, while an Omani delegation shuttles through Tehran on Friday and Saturday trying to negotiate a provisional arrangement for vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz; a regional official calls the pause 'a positive signal that helps their efforts to de-escalate,' White House communications director Steven Cheung says President Trump 'has always been consistent in saying he prefers a diplomatic solution,' and Netanyahu says he fully backs the pressure campaign while warning Iran against attacking Israel again, though the US naval blockade stays in force with a dozen commercial ships redirected and two boarded

An oil tanker explodes in the Strait of Hormuz after deviating from the navigation corridor designated by Iranian authorities and striking a naval mine, according to Iranian outlet Defa Press, with no independent information released on the ship's identity, flag, ownership or casualties; over the same 24 hours the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy intercepts six vessels attempting what it calls unauthorised transit of the waterway, firing warning shots to force them to turn back, after Tehran suspended its own fee-free corridor over US attempts to escort ships through it

The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification reports that 1.2 million people in Gaza, 59 percent of the population, faced crisis-level hunger or worse from mid-April to the end of June, including about 212,000 in the emergency phase, with all five governorates classified at Phase 3; two-thirds of the population is projected to be in crisis by year's end, 1.4 million people face high acute food insecurity through December, and roughly 74,200 children under five are expected to need treatment for acute malnutrition through April 2027, with the IPC calling gains since the October 2025 ceasefire real but 'deeply fragile'

Russia fires seven ballistic missiles and 136 drones at Ukraine overnight, striking Kyiv and setting fires on the upper floors of apartment buildings in the central district, then continuing through the day: a drone hits a supermarket in Chernihiv killing two people including a 10-year-old child, one person is killed and 12 wounded in a daytime drone attack on Kharkiv, and a glide bomb kills one and wounds six in Zaporizhzhia, while the Russian-installed mayor of Horlivka says a Ukrainian drone strike killed four civilians there; President Zelensky calls the barrage 'deliberate Russian terror that has no military justification'

Berlin police shoot dead 21-year-old Abdul Ballout in the Spandau district after a manhunt, ending a search that followed Saturday night's attack in which he drove a van into crowds in Tiergarten park near the Christopher Street Day Pride route and then stabbed people with a bladed weapon, killing one and injuring 29, some with life-threatening wounds; Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says 'everything we see here indicates that this was an Islamist terror attack,' the suspect had been convicted of preparing a serious act of subversive violence after seeking to join ISIL, and Mayor Kai Wegner calls it 'an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society'

Wildfires in France and Spain force more than a quarter of a million people from their homes, with 220,000 evacuated in the Gironde alone plus 36,000 in the Landes and nearly 3,000 in the Var, roughly 42,000 hectares burned around Bordeaux, hundreds of homes destroyed and 75 firefighters treated for injuries, while Spain has 76,000 evacuated, 30,000 confined indoors and one death in Manises outside Valencia; Interior Minister Laurent Nunez says 'the situation remains very unfavorable' after 'another difficult night,' fire chief Marc Vermeulen compares the blaze to 'being confronted by a hurricane,' and forecasters warn of hotter weather returning from Tuesday

The Bundibugyo-virus Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo passes 3,075 confirmed cases and 1,354 deaths, with the toll up about 40 percent in five days and cases up 27 percent week on week, more than 100 health workers infected and roughly 35 killed; it is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record, reaching 1,000 deaths in under 10 weeks against eight months for the 2013-2016 West African epidemic, and public health consultant Abdulsalami Nasidi says the virus 'is spreading like a wildfire' with no approved vaccine or treatment, though Oxford researchers began trials of an experimental Bundibugyo vaccine on July 24

Sudan's army says it has retaken the town of Bara and four nearby villages, Al Barakah, Umm Sayalah, Jobret Al Sheikh and Umm Qarfah, after fierce battles with the Rapid Support Forces, securing a supply route to the besieged army garrison in Al Obeid some 50km away and extending control over the road linking North Kordofan to Omdurman; the military claims heavy RSF losses and abandoned weapons, figures that cannot be independently verified, in a war that has displaced roughly 14 million people

The Vietnamese cargo ship Khoi Nguyen 18 sinks late Saturday in bad weather near Fiery Cross Reef in the contested Spratly Islands with 62 people aboard, leaving 45 rescued and 17 missing as Vietnamese, Philippine and Chinese vessels and aircraft mount a joint multinational search; Vietnam's foreign ministry spokesperson Pham Thu Hang confirms the vessel went down in what Hanoi calls the East Sea, and the Philippine Coast Guard deploys a patrol ship and aircraft at Vietnam's request

Three people are killed and four wounded, including a two-year-old child, in a shooting at Seattle Center around 6pm on the final day of the Bite of Seattle food festival, with the dead a 19-year-old man, a 44-year-old man and a 56-year-old woman; police believe multiple shooters exchanged fire in an apparently gang-related confrontation, recover two firearms and take one suspect into custody, and Mayor Katie Wilson calls it an 'act of horrific violence,' adding that 'no one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event'

Brent crude is up roughly 24 percent since fighting resumed on July 8, trading between about 97 and 102 dollars a barrel through the week, a milder rally than the 43 percent surge of the war's opening weeks as supply buffers and political calculation cap the move, while pump prices climb again and energy companies post record quarterly profits; separately China protests EU sanctions on Chinese firms accused of supporting Russia and retaliates by placing 14 EU entities under export controls, insisting its position on Ukraine is 'objective and just'

The Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft lands safely on the Kazakh steppe near Dzhezkazgan at 5:27am CDT, returning NASA astronaut Chris Williams and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev after 241 days in orbit, 3,856 revolutions of the Earth and more than 102 million miles travelled; the parachute-assisted touchdown closes out Expedition 74 aboard the International Space Station and hands over to Expedition 75, capping a week that also saw SpaceX fly its Starship on a 13th test flight from Starbase on July 24
